item.title: Optimizely supply chain attack, AI-built exploits, Project Zero
item.description:
A supply chain attack on Optimizely put malicious scripts on well-known websites, and Google reports an AI agent that turned patches into exploits without human help. Also: Project Zero shortens its disclosure deadlines, the Barracuda and Uber breaches, California's lawsuit against OpenAI, and Microsoft's explanation of its email outage.

Stories covered:

  • Optimizely supply chain attack hits major brand sites — Sources: BleepingComputer, Techmeme
  • Google: AI agent turned patches into working exploits — Sources: The Register Security, The Next Web
  • Project Zero shortens bug disclosure deadlines — Sources: BleepingComputer, Dark Reading, The Next Web, Techmeme
  • Barracuda breach tied to ARTEX AI framework — Sources: BleepingComputer, TechCrunch, The Register Security
  • Uber says Fireworks AI breach exposed driver licenses — Sources: TechCrunch
  • California sues OpenAI over rogue agent incidents — Sources: TechCrunch, The Record, BleepingComputer, Techmeme, BleepingComputer
  • Microsoft blames 365 outage on July software defect — Sources: Hacker News, The Next Web, Ars Technica, The Register

item.title: Nvidia CEO Huang resigns, Cursor extension attack, FBI warns of ARTEX
item.description:
Today's brief covers Jensen Huang's exit as Nvidia CEO, the Cursor and Fireworks A I incident behind a tampered Claude Code extension, and an F B I warning about the ARTEX attack framework. It also covers an A W S sign-in outage in US East one and a data breach at France's Maileva.

Stories covered:

  • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down amid spy scandal — Sources: The Verge AI, The Verge
  • Stolen key led to tampered Claude Code extension in Cursor — Sources: The Hacker News
  • FBI warns ARTEX A I tool is automating cyberattacks — Sources: BleepingComputer
  • AWS sign-in and connectivity errors in US-EAST-1 — Sources: AWS Status
  • Cyberattack on La Poste unit exposes data of 22 million — Sources: DataBreaches.net
